narratives.Overview:
Four defects found while running a full seventeen-story delivery programme on Directive 0.104.0, on a private consumer project. None blocked delivery — workarounds are given for each — but each cost time, and three of the four share one root cause: **the v0.6 → v0.8 rename was applied to some surfaces and not others.**

Everything below was re-verified against the installed 0.104.0 deposit immediately before filing, with file and line references. Where our original internal notes were wrong, the corrected finding is what appears here, and the correction is called out.

> **Edited after filing.** All four were then checked against the `v0.105.0` tag — the current release — and **all four still reproduce there**; per-defect evidence is in the first comment. Defect 3 below has also been rewritten: the original diagnosis (a file missing from the consumer deposit) was wrong, and the real one is worse. Nothing else has changed.

**Environment**

| | |
|---|---|
| `@deftai/directive` | 0.104.0 |
| `@deftai/directive-core` | 0.104.0 |
| `@deftai/directive-content` | 0.104.0 |
| Node | v22.15.0 |
| OS / shell | Windows 11, Git Bash |
| Repository default branch | `main` |
| xBRIEF layout | v0.8 (`xbrief/`) |

---

## 1. `spec:render` rejects v0.8 — two copies of the same constant have diverged

### Reproduce

```
deft spec:render xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json out.md
```

```
✗ PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json has schema violations:
  • missing required top-level key 'vBRIEFInfo'
```

The project's own `PROJECT-DEFINITION`, generated by `deft-directive-setup` at v0.8, is rejected by `spec:render`.

### Root cause

There are two schema validators, and only one was migrated.

| File | Accepts |
|---|---|
| `dist/vbrief-validate/schema.js:114` | `'vBRIEFInfo' or 'xBRIEFInfo'` — migrated for #2107 |
| `dist/render/spec-validate.js:50` | `'vBRIEFInfo'` only — **not migrated** |

The version constant has diverged the same way:

```js
// dist/vbrief-validate/constants.js:17
export const VALID_VBRIEF_VERSIONS = new Set(["0.6", "0.8"]);

// dist/render/constants.js:13
export const VALID_VBRIEF_VERSIONS = new Set(["0.6"]);
```

`render/spec-validate.js:59` still emits the pre-#2107 message — *"must be '0.6' (canonical v0.6 schema, #533)"* — where `vbrief-validate/schema.js:118` emits the current *"canonical v0.6/v0.8 schema, #2107"*. So even with the key accepted, the version check would reject `0.8` on the render path.

**How we found it:** ran the command, grepped `dist/` for the literal error string, then compared the two validators side by side.

### Proposed fix

Either have `render/` import the constant and the info-key resolver from `vbrief-validate/`, or apply the #2107 change to `render/spec-validate.js` and `render/constants.js`. The first is preferable — two hand-maintained copies of one schema rule will diverge again on the next rename.

Worth checking whether other `render/` consumers (`project-render.js`, `roadmap-render.js`) resolve the info key correctly; both reference `vBRIEFInfo`.

### Workaround

`SPECIFICATION.md` is rendered directly from the narratives, with a header note recording why and when to switch back.

---

## 2. `swarm:finalize-cohort` prints the right delivery branch and then fetches the wrong one

### Reproduce

On any repository whose default branch is `main`:

```
git fetch origin master failed: fatal: couldn't find remote ref master
cohort completion sweep failed.
```

The command reports the delivery branch correctly first. Running it with `--help`:

```
Swarm cohort finalize live (0 stories)
  Project root: <path>
  Delivery branch: main
  ...
```

**It resolves `main`, and then fetches `master`.**

### Root cause

```js
// dist/swarm/finalize-cohort.js:319
const baseBranch = args.baseBranch ?? "master";

// dist/swarm/finalize-cohort-cli.js:9
let baseBranch = "master";

// dist/swarm/finalize-cohort.js:193
const fetch = runGit(["git", "fetch", "origin", baseBranch], { cwd: projectRoot });
```

The fallback is the string literal `"master"`, not the resolved delivery branch. The resolver already exists and does the right thing — `dist/policy/delivery-branch.js:58`, `resolveDeliveryBranch()`, ordering typed `plan.policy.deliveryBranch` → git remote default → local `main`/`master` → fallback. `dist/lifecycle/completed-tracked-on-delivery.js:194` calls it. `finalize-cohort` does not.

### Two corrections to our original internal note

1. **`--base-branch` does exist** (`finalize-cohort-cli.js:51`). Our note said there was no override; that was wrong. The real problem is that it is undiscoverable, because —
2. **`--help` is not handled at all.** It is not recognised as a flag, so the command *runs* with an empty cohort and prints its normal output. On a command that pushes and opens a PR, an unrecognised `--help` executing rather than printing usage is worth fixing on its own.

We also could **not** reproduce this on `scope:complete` in 0.104.0. `dist/scope/delivery-evidence.js:252` takes `deliveryBranch` from the resolved `branchResult.branch`, with a comment citing #3041 — *"Policy/git-default is SoT"*. It looks fixed there; the fix appears not to have reached `finalize-cohort`.

### Proposed fix

- `finalize-cohort.js:319` and `finalize-cohort-cli.js:9`: default to `resolveDeliveryBranch(projectRoot)` rather than `"master"`, keeping `--base-branch` as the explicit override.
- Handle `--help` / `-h` in `finalize-cohort-cli.js` and return before any side effect.
- Consider a test asserting that no command fetches a branch other than the one it just reported.

### Workaround

The lifecycle-PR path that `commands.md` names as the sanctioned alternative, with delivery verified independently — every PR `MERGED`, every merge commit confirmed an ancestor of `origin/main`.

## 3. The probe strategy mandates a script that was deleted when the guard was ported to TypeScript

*(Originally filed as "missing from the consumer deposit". That was wrong — the file is not missing from the deposit, it does not exist anywhere in the project any more.)*

### Evidence

`content/strategies/probe.md:76–99` makes the script mandatory, with `!` (MUST) directives:

```
### Mechanical guard (`scripts/probe_session.py`)
! At probe start, record the session:
  `uv run python scripts/probe_session.py start --target <scope>`
! Immediately before artifact or plan registration, run the guard:
  - `uv run python scripts/probe_session.py guard-artifact --path ...`
  - `uv run python scripts/probe_session.py guard-plan-registration`
⊗ Write probe artifacts or update `completedStrategies.probe` while the
  session state is still `interrogate`
```

But `scripts/probe_session.py` returns **404 at `v0.105.0`**, and it is present in neither the consumer deposit nor any installed `@deftai/*` package.

A code search shows why: **the guard was ported to TypeScript.** It now lives at `packages/core/src/orchestration/probe-session.ts`, with the port recorded in `xbrief/completed/2026-06-19-port-subagent-monitor-investigation-gates-to-ts.xbrief.json` and `xbrief/completed/2026-06-09-add-mechanical-guardrails-against-premature-probe-completion.xbrief.json`. `packages/cli/src/orchestration-cli/coverage-map.ts` still lists `test_probe_session.py`, which is what first suggested the Python file was merely unshipped.

`probe.md` was never updated to match. A code search for `probe:session` returns no CLI verb, so if the ported guard is reachable from the command line it is not discoverable by name.

**Net effect: every agent running `probe` is instructed, as a MUST, to invoke a file deleted two months ago — and marked `⊗` for proceeding without it.** The strategy is unrunnable as written, and the failure is silent, because an agent that cannot run the guard either stops or quietly substitutes its own judgement.

### Proposed fix

Update `probe.md` to invoke the TypeScript guard, and expose it as a named verb if it is not already one. If the guard is intentionally maintainer-only, say so in the strategy and give consumers a documented fallback rather than a `⊗`.

A completeness check — every path or script named in a shipped strategy resolves — would catch this and defect #4 together, and would catch the next rename.

### Workaround

Transition criteria were met by inspection, and the substitution was recorded in the probe artifact rather than passed over silently.

---

## 4. Fifteen shipped strategy documents still instruct agents to write to `vbrief/` paths

This one was not in our original notes. It surfaced while verifying #1 and #3, and we think it is the most consequential of the four.

### Evidence

The framework renamed the layout to `xbrief/`, and the managed AGENTS.md section says so — *"Legacy `vbrief/` read-accepted; `deft migrate:xbrief` for `xbrief/` (v0.6→v0.8)"*. But the shipped strategies were not updated. Counting `vbrief/` occurrences under `.deft/core/strategies/`:

| File | Refs | | File | Refs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `speckit.md` | 48 | | `research.md` | 6 |
| `interview.md` | 22 | | `map.md` | 5 |
| `enterprise.md` | 18 | | `README.md` | 4 |
| `v0-20-contract.md` | 18 | | `roadmap.md` | 1 |
| `rapid.md` | 16 | | `artifact-guards.md` | 6 |
| `yolo.md` | 13 | | `bdd.md` | 6 |
| `discuss.md` | 8 | | `emit-hints.md` | 8 |
| `probe.md` | 8 | | | |

`discuss.md` is representative — it instructs, with `!` (MUST):

```
! Produce a `vbrief/proposed/{scope}-context.vbrief.json` scope vBRIEF
  with a `LockedDecisions` narrative
! On completion, register artifacts in `./vbrief/plan.vbrief.json`
```

`probe.md` additionally refers to `PROJECT-DEFINITION.vbrief.json`, which on a v0.8 project is `PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json`.

### Why it matters

These documents are read by agents and followed literally. An agent running `discuss` on a v0.8 project either writes to a `vbrief/` directory that should not exist, or silently substitutes the right path and diverges from the instruction it was given. Neither is good: the first splits the project's artifacts across two layouts, and the second makes the contract advisory rather than mechanical — which is exactly what the strategies' own `⊗` markers exist to prevent.

Same root cause as #1: the rename reached the validators and the AGENTS.md managed section, but not the strategy corpus.

### Proposed fix

Migrate the strategy corpus to `xbrief/` paths (source of truth appears to be `packs/strategies/strategies-pack-0.1.json`, with `task packs:render` regenerating the markdown), and add a check that no shipped strategy references a legacy path once the rename is complete.

---

## Not a defect, but worth knowing

The PreToolUse hook resolves ritual state from the **parent repository path** rather than the active git worktree — `dist/session/ritual-sentinel.js:13` anchors state at `<projectRoot>/.deft/ritual-state.json`. Agents working inside a worktree must run `deft session:ready` against the parent before file writes are permitted. Observed during the programme; not re-verified in this pass, since no worktree was active. Surprising rather than wrong, and easy to lose time to.

---

Happy to open separate issues per defect if you would rather track them individually, or to test a fix on this project — it is a real v0.8 consumer on Windows with a `main` default branch, which appears to be the combination that surfaces all four.

### 1. `spec:render` rejects v0.8 -- accurate, slightly oversold as a greenfield blocker

The split is real:

- `packages/core/src/vbrief-validate/constants.ts` -- `VALID_VBRIEF_VERSIONS = {0.6, 0.8}`, accepts `vBRIEFInfo` or `xBRIEFInfo`
- `packages/core/src/render/constants.ts` -- still `{0.6}` only
- `packages/core/src/render/spec-validate.ts:55-65` -- still requires `vBRIEFInfo` and still emits the pre-#2107 *"must be '0.6' (#533)"* message

That is leftover from #2107, which only migrated the main validator.

Caveat on the reproduce command:

```
deft spec:render xbrief/PROJECT-DEFINITION.xbrief.json out.md
```

`spec:render` is documented to render `xbrief/specification.xbrief.json`, not PROJECT-DEFINITION. Greenfield v0.20/v0.8 trees are supposed to use `task project:export-spec`. That path **does not** run `validateSpec` on PROJECT-DEFINITION; it only calls it for a `full-spec` tree that has `specification.xbrief.json`.

So:

- Greenfield PD-only: `project:export-spec` should work. Hitting `spec:render` on PROJECT-DEFINITION is the wrong verb.
- Full-spec / migrated tree with a v0.8 `specification.xbrief.json`: **both** `spec:render` and `project:export-spec` fail, because export-spec uses the same stale validator on that path.

`project-render` already chooses `xBRIEFInfo` vs `vBRIEFInfo` by layout (#2149). `roadmap-render` already walks both keys. Those two "worth checking" notes are already done.

**Need:** fix `render/spec-validate` to share `vbrief-validate`'s info-key + version set. Small, high-leverage. Do not treat the PROJECT-DEFINITION reproduce as the primary consumer path.

### 2. `finalize-cohort` prints `main`, fetches `master` -- accurate, highest need

This is the one to fix first.

- `resolveDeliveryBranch()` is used for **delivery proof** and is what the command prints (`Delivery branch: main`).
- `baseBranch` is a **separate** knob for the lifecycle-sweep PR (#3041). Default is still the literal `"master"` in both `finalize-cohort.ts:448` and `finalize-cohort-cli.ts:12`.
- `syncBaseBranch` then `git fetch origin ${baseBranch}` / `git merge --ff-only origin/${baseBranch}`.

The report's "resolves main then fetches master" is observationally right, slightly imprecise on mechanism: it is not that the resolver is ignored for delivery; the sweep base never uses the resolver.

`--base-branch` exists. `--help` / `-h` do not -- unknown flags are dropped, so `--help` runs a live empty-cohort finalize. That is a real CLI bug on a mutating command. Smaller than the fetch, still worth the same PR.

`scope:complete` using resolved delivery branch is consistent with current source (`delivery-evidence` / #3041). That correction in the report is right.

**Need:** high. This is the sanctioned post-merge land path (`swarm:finalize-cohort` / lifecycle PR) on any repo whose default branch is `main`. Workaround is `--base-branch main`, which operators cannot discover from `--help`. Independent of the rename; do not bury it inside a strategy-doc cleanup.

### 3. Probe guard -- diagnosis in the follow-up comment is right; "no CLI" is not

`scripts/probe_session.py` is gone. `content/strategies/probe.md:76-99` still `!` mandates:

```
uv run python scripts/probe_session.py start --target <scope>
uv run python scripts/probe_session.py guard-artifact --path vbrief/proposed/...
```

and `⊗` proceeding without it.

The TypeScript port is live: `packages/core/src/orchestration/probe-session.ts`, dispatched as **`deft probe-session`** (hyphen) via `packages/cli/src/dispatch.ts`. There is no `task probe:session` and no `probe:session` colon verb, which is why a search for `probe:session` returned nothing.

Worse, the error strings in the TS module still tell you to run the deleted Python file (`probe-session.ts:300`, `:376`, `:386`). And `strategy_chaining.test.ts` **asserts** that `probe.md` contains `scripts/probe_session.py` and `probe_session.py complete`. Updating the strategy without changing that test fails closed on the *wrong* contract.

**Need:** high if anyone actually runs `probe`; otherwise docs/test rot. The code exists. The product gap is: strategy pack + error strings + content-contract tests still describe a deleted script, and the live verb is undiscoverable by the name agents will search.

Source of truth is `content/packs/strategies/strategies-pack-0.1.json` + `task packs:render`. Editing the rendered `.md` files is the wrong fix.

A "path must resolve" check would catch defect 3 (`probe_session.py` 404). It would **not** catch defect 4: `vbrief/` can still be created. ## Design critique of the triage comment (checked at `0b212e25a0fd0097bed5df5c6b804129f45d3b0d`)

Independent pass over the triage above (Keep / three children / defect 2 first). Load-bearing line cites re-verified against this SHA. Classification: **blocks-the-design** / **sharpens-framing** / **footnote**.

### What holds

- Defects 1–3 code cites are accurate at this SHA: `render/constants.ts` still `Set(["0.6"])`; `render/spec-validate.ts:55–65` still requires `vBRIEFInfo` and the pre-#2107 version message; `finalize-cohort.ts:448` and `finalize-cohort-cli.ts:12` still default `"master"` while `resolveDeliveryBranch()` feeds the printed delivery branch; `probe.md` still `!`-mandates `scripts/probe_session.py`; `dispatch.ts` registers `probe-session`; `strategy_chaining.test.ts:201` / `:218` still assert the deleted script strings; probe-session error strings still teach the Python CLI (`probe-session.ts:300`, `:334`, `:352`, `:376`, `:386–387` — triage named three of five).
- Splitting rename leftovers from the hardcoded-`master` land-path bug is right. Tracker ≠ one story is right (propose-not-apply).
- Rejecting a naive “path must resolve” check for defect 4 is right: `vbrief/` can still be created.
- `project-render` layout awareness (#2149) and `roadmap-render` walking both envelope keys are already done; the reporter’s “worth checking” notes are spent.

### Findings

1. **[blocks-the-design] Pack child (3+4) is a multi-surface wall, not a thin first ship (#3265).**  
   The triage’s child 3 bundles: pack SoT edit (`strategies-pack-0.1.json` + `packs:render`), corpus rewrite across many strategies, probe error-string retarget in TS, content-contract retarget, *and* a new layout-aware strategy-path contract. Thin fail-closed wants one deterministic check + one remediation for the first close, with optional complexity deferred. Under a headless / hostile envelope, that bundle is exactly the blast-radius shape that stalls or half-lands. Prefer: (a) land defect 2 alone as already ranked; (b) one thin gate (e.g. “every `!`-named CLI/script token in shipped strategies resolves on the live dispatch map” **or** “MUST-write lifecycle roots match live layout”) with a single remediation string; (c) corpus migration as a follow-up child, not the same unit of work as the gate.

2. **[blocks-the-design] “Retarget `strategy_chaining.test.ts` first” is gate-integrity-hazardous if read as weaken-then-fix (#3156).**  
   Today the content contract **fail-closes on the wrong product** (asserts the deleted Python path). That inverted gate is real. The safe close is **atomic same-PR**: product (strategy + error strings + verb discovery) and contract assertion move together. Ordering “change the test first” so the probe update can land invites clearing red by editing the verifier — the gate-integrity anti-pattern — especially under swarm where a leaf may only get the test half of the envelope.

3. **[blocks-the-design] Probe “need” must not be usage-contingent.**
